% An article as LaTeX's standard classes set it, with no layout package:
% two abstracts, headings, lists (an item that starts with a list or ends in
% a block), a figure's caption, a footnote, inline TikZ pictures (one with
% \, in a node), the LaTeX logo, and a bibliography.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{tikz}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\title{An article}
\author{Someone}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
A short abstract.
\end{abstract}
\begin{abstract}
A second, as in another language.
\end{abstract}
\section{Lists}
Text with a footnote.\footnote{A note, \emph{emphasized}.}
\begin{itemize}
    \item One,
    \begin{itemize}
        \item inside.
    \end{itemize}
    \item[$\star$] A label of its own.
\end{itemize}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item First,
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item inside.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\begin{itemize}
    \item[Case 1] \begin{itemize} \item a list in an item at once. \end{itemize}
    \item Ends centered.
    \begin{center} Centered. \end{center}
    \item Ends in a theorem.
    \begin{theorem} A theorem. \end{theorem}
\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
    \item[Term] A description long enough to run onto a second line, which
    \LaTeX\ indents by the list's left margin, as it does every item.
\end{description}
\subsection{Pictures}
A ball \tikz{\fill (0,0) circle (0.5);} in the text, as cited in \cite{book}.
A node with a thin space, \tikz\node{10\,000};, as wide as in the PDF.
\begin{figure}
    \centering
    \rule{1cm}{1cm}
    \caption{A square.}
\end{figure}
\begin{thebibliography}{9}
\bibitem{book} A.~Author. \emph{A Book}. 2000.
\end{thebibliography}
\end{document}
